claim_being_audited: That the model should be certified for launch on the current record as a policy-compliant and evidentially supported decision.
decision_criteria: Use policy text as the controlling standard, not general public governance principles.
Treat named customer commitments and named launch use cases as materiality triggers.
Do not treat 'non-core' or low projected volume as sufficient to negate materiality where policy says otherwise.
Require admissible evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before finding certification compliant.
Distinguish technical launch readiness from policy compliance; both are required for a compliant certification decision.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering the named launch use case before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the underwriting support gap must be disclosed.
Evidence that the gap has been resolved or reduced so it is no longer a material limitation for the named launch use case.
Launch materials or model-card disclosure showing the limitation was in fact disclosed for the named commitments.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and a clean severity-one rehearsal support launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure predicate in the release policy.

The affected credit underwriting support segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two lender rollout commitments, which makes the limitation plausibly material under the policy text.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no admissible evidence shows either condition was met.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy determination remains unresolved.
Product's 'non-core' or low-volume framing is expressly insufficient to resolve materiality when named commitments or pending legal review exist.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record despite the unresolved disclosure requirement.
That public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring is sufficient support for certification when an internal policy predicate remains unmet.
Any implication that the current record adequately supports certification without either disclosure, resolution of the gap, or approved risk acceptance.
